exercise.name: Side Plank Clamshell

reference.title: Side Plank Clamshell (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (side bridge on the knee plus top-hip abduction and external rotation)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the hips lift and the knee opens, inhale as you close and lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.8 s open, 0.6 s hold, 0.8 s close, 1 s down

prescription.tempo: About 1 s up, open, pause, close, 1 s down
prescription.progression: Mini band above the knees, then hold the top longer, then a straight-leg side plank with abduction

cues.text: Lie on the right side, right elbow under the shoulder, hips and knees bent, feet together behind you.
Breathe out, press the forearm and bottom knee into the mat and lift the hips.
With the hips up, open the top knee like a clamshell, feet staying together.
Shoulders, hips and knees in one line; hips stacked, not rolling back.
Breathe in and lower the hips to the mat; repeat, then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Pelvis rolling back as the knee opens
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips stacked; open only as far as the pelvis stays still.
Press the bottom knee and forearm down; keep the line from shoulders to knees.
Push the floor away with the forearm; elbow under the shoulder.
Keep the feet together; the knee opens, the feet stay stacked.

kinematics.setup: Hips on the mat, trunk side-bent 38° toward the ceiling
kinematics.peak: Shoulder-hip-knee ≈35° off straight (hips flexed 30° forward of the line)
kinematics.norm: Shoulders, hips and knees in one line at the top (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: On the mat under the shoulder, forearm pointing forward
kinematics.norm: Elbow under the shoulder, forearm on the mat (clinical opinion)
Pelvis lifts off the mat into the side bridge (Boren 2011 side plank with abduction)

kinematics.peak: Top knee opens 40° about the hip-ankle axis (knees 29 cm apart; hip abd 10.8°, rot -16.9°)
kinematics.norm: Knee opens with the feet together; Selkowitz 2013 and Boren 2011 used clams with the hips flexed

kinematics.peak: Bottom knee and shin stay on the mat; the feet stay together
kinematics.norm: Knees bent about 90 degrees, feet stacked (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1 s lift, 0.8 s open, 0.6 s hold, 0.8 s close, 1 s lower, 0.8 s rest
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1 s for each movement (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #984912, Side Plank Clamshell (male), video (movement reference)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

Selkowitz, Beneck & Powers 2013, which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Fine-wire EMG of 11 exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(2):54-64)
Macadam, Cronin & Contreras 2015, gluteal muscle activity in dynamic hip abduction and hip external rotation exercise: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 10(5):573-591; PMC4595911)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Shoulder pain on the support side: build up with the side-lying clam first.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: lower the hips between reps for longer, or do side-lying clams.
Knee discomfort: pad the bottom knee.
regressions: Kneeling side plank hold without the clam.
progressions: Straight-leg side plank with top-leg abduction.

muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Top leg: opens the knee (abduction and external rotation in hip flexion). The clam reached about 27% MVIC gluteus medius with low TFL (Selkowitz 2013); clam progressions ranged about 47-77% MVIC in Boren 2011.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Bottom leg: holds the pelvis up in the side bridge. Side plank with abduction reached about 89-103% MVIC gluteus medius in Boren 2011, among the highest of 18 exercises.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Upper fibres help the clam (about 44% MVIC superior gluteus maximus in Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Lift and hold the hips off the mat (side bridge; clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the body in one line from shoulders to knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Bottom side: helps keep the hips extended in line (Boren 2011 side plank data; clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Support shoulder: pushes the forearm into the mat so the shoulder does not sag (clinical opinion).
